title: Life after a heart attack
what: After a heart attack, the heart takes several months to recover. Medicines, activity, and quitting smoking lower the risk of another one.
why: For everyone who has had a heart attack, and for their family.
duration: recovery usually takes several weeks to months
tell_doctor: If chest pain or pressure comes back
If it is hard to take your medicines or they cause side effects
Ask when you can go back to work, driving, and sex

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Usually several medicines are prescribed for a long time. Take them every day and do not stop on your own.

prepare.title: Rehabilitation
prepare.text: Ask about a cardiac rehab program. It helps you return to activity safely.

prepare.title: Under-the-tongue medicine
prepare.text: Ask your doctor if you need a medicine for chest pain and how to take it.

bring: A diary of your blood pressure and pulse
steps: Take your medicines every day at the same time
Start with short walks and slowly do more
Eat less salt and fat, and more vegetables
Measure your blood pressure and pulse and write them down
Go to all your follow-up visits
feel: Tiredness in the first weeks is common
Fear and anxiety after a heart attack are a normal reaction, and you can tell your doctor about them
after: Cholesterol and sugar tests follow your doctor's schedule
Going back to work and sport is your doctor's decision
Teach your family how to recognize a heart attack
red_flags: Chest pain or pressure lasting more than a few minutes: call emergency services
Pain spreading to the arm, jaw, or back, or a cold sweat: call emergency services
Severe shortness of breath or fainting: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I have sex after a heart attack?
faq.a: Usually yes, once your doctor allows physical activity. Ask your doctor directly.

faq.q: Why shouldn't I stop my pills if I feel fine?
faq.a: They protect your heart and blood vessels from another heart attack. Feeling well is not a reason to stop.

reminders.text: Time for your heart medicine. Then a calm walk.
